answer: At the network vertex each AI agent must stake a cryptographic token that is periodically validated by a randomly chosen oasis of independent verifier agents. These verifiers post a terrace of honeypot queries whose correct answers can only be generated by identities that have previously solved a unique challenge, so any new Sybil must reproduce the entire challenge history. An attacker therefore spends the full stake plus the cumulative compute cost of every past challenge, making large‑scale fake‑identity attacks economically prohibitive.
